questions.question: If hazardous materials catch fire in your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Wait for the fire to go out on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire is dangerous. You need special training and protective gear. Do not try to fight the fire yourself unless you have this equipment and training.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label is too large to fit on the package?

options.text: Put the label on a tag that is securely attached to the package.
Attach a QR code to be scanned instead.
Make the label smaller so it fits on the package.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the label on a tag that is securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If a hazard warning label will not fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package instead.

questions.question: What equipment must you have in your vehicle when transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine in cargo tanks, you must have an approved gas mask in your vehicle.

questions.question: How should you warn others when transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: Display hazardous materials placards on your truck.
Use flashing lights on your truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Display hazardous materials placards on your truck.
questions.explanation: You must display diamond-shaped warning signs (placards) on vehicles transporting hazardous materials. You must also provide shipping papers and emergency response information.

questions.question: Explosive materials are most likely classified as a ____ hazard.
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are items that can explode or catch fire.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: How much packaging is needed for shipping.
Where on the trailer the material can be placed.
The correct way to load and unload the material.

questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. A material's hazard class identifies what dangers it poses.

questions.question: When you apply for a new or renewed hazardous materials endorsement, which agency conducts the background check?
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) performs a federal security threat assessment for all new and renewed hazardous materials endorsement applications.

questions.question: Flammable gases are classified as ____ hazards.
questions.explanation: Flammable gases are classified as Class 2 hazardous materials.

questions.question: What should you do when loading or unloading explosive materials?

options.text: Use sharp tools to open packages.

questions.explanation: Always turn off your engine before loading or unloading explosives. Never drop, throw, or roll packages containing explosives.

questions.question: How long must shippers keep a copy of hazardous materials shipping papers?
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy of hazardous materials shipping papers for at least two years after the initial carrier accepts the materials. For hazardous waste, the requirement is three years.

questions.question: A person watching a tank being loaded or unloaded must do all of the following, except:

options.text: Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Know the hazards of the materials.

questions.explanation: The person supervising tank loading or unloading must be alert, have a clear view of the tank, stay within 25 feet of the tank, know the material hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: The only correct way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tires with your hand.

questions.explanation: Check each tire at the start of every trip. Using a tire pressure gauge is the only reliable way to check if tire pressure is correct.

questions.question: Shipping papers:

options.text: Are not needed for most shipments.
Should be stored in a special spot in the cab.
Can be kept as a digital file only.

questions.explanation: Shipping papers are required for all hazardous materials shipments. They inform drivers and dockworkers about the risks of the cargo.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.1 materials, the floor liner must be made from:
questions.explanation: When transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials, use a tight floor liner made from non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal. Non-ferrous metals do not contain iron or iron alloys.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, it is important to know that:

options.text: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
The package should be placed in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.
The package should be made of wood.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation will pass through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads out from each radioactive package and passes through nearby packages. The number of packages that can be loaded together is limited.

questions.question: A driver needs a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to transport hazardous materials in:

options.text: A vehicle requiring a Class A license.
A vehicle requiring a Class B license.
A vehicle requiring a Class C license.

questions.explanation: You must have a CDL with a hazardous materials endorsement to drive any vehicle that carries hazardous materials.

questions.question: How are hazardous materials warnings shown?

options.text: By wrapping the package in orange
By placing the item away from other cargo and covering it with a sign

questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on vehicles and packages to warn drivers and others about hazardous materials.

questions.question: The only correct way to check tire pressure is by:

options.text: Pushing on the tire with your hand.
Measuring the height of the tire.

questions.explanation: Check your tires at the start of every trip and after every stop. A tire pressure gauge is the only acceptable way to check if tire pressure is correct.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials. Someone must stay at the nozzle and control the fuel flow at all times while refueling.

questions.question: Do not smoke within ____ of a vehicle with placards for Class 3 or Division 2.1 materials.
questions.explanation: Do not smoke within 25 feet of a placarded cargo tank carrying Class 3 (flammable liquids) or Division 2.1 (gases) materials. Do not smoke or carry a lit cigar, pipe, or cigarette near flammable or explosive materials.

questions.question: Who must mark and label materials for shipping?
questions.explanation: The shipper must warn drivers and others about hazardous materials. They do this by putting hazard labels on packages, putting placards on vehicles, and providing shipping papers and emergency information.

questions.question: When transporting explosives, what must you do?

options.text: You must have a written route plan.
You should take the shortest possible route.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must have a written route plan.
questions.explanation: When transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, you must follow a written route plan. Avoid heavily populated areas, crowds, tunnels, narrow streets, and alleys. Research any restrictions for your planned routes.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained and tested?
questions.explanation: All drivers must be trained about security risks of hazardous materials. This includes recognizing and responding to security threats. Training and testing must happen at least once every three years.

questions.question: Where should placards be placed on a truck?

options.text: On the left and right sides

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: What does "Forbidden" mean in the third column of the Hazardous Materials Table?

options.text: The substance should not be transported.
The substance should be transported by air.
The substance should only be transported at night.
The substance should be accompanied by a security guard.

questions.correctAnswerText: The substance should not be transported.
questions.explanation: The third column of the Hazardous Materials Table lists hazard classes and divisions. Never transport a material marked as "Forbidden."

questions.question: If a package says "Inhalation Hazard," which placard must be used?
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a package or shipping paper, display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard.

questions.question: What must emergency response information from the shipper include?

options.text: Any risks of fire or explosion.
How many people should respond in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any risks of fire or explosion.
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must include: descriptions and names of materials; health hazards; risks of fire or explosion; precautions for accidents; methods for handling fires; methods for handling spills or leaks; and first aid measures.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Check to see if the doors are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check to see if the doors are hot.
questions.explanation: Feel the doors first to check if they are hot. If the doors are hot, there may be a cargo fire inside. Keep the doors closed if there is a cargo fire.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The manual covers exam material but not all job safety information. Hazardous materials training courses provide additional knowledge needed to transport hazardous materials safely.

questions.question: What could indicate that a shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is packaged in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums often contain hazardous materials. Take proper precautions when transporting cargo in these containers.
